submitted.rationale: Index 46 (Ca0.19 Cu0.18 V0.63) had the highest EQE measured, 0.130%. EQE rose steadily as V went up and Cu went down across the three measurements. This fits a V-rich Cu vanadate / V2O5-type absorber with a gap near the 2.06 eV photon energy.

rejected.reason: Cu-rich (Cu 0.54). EQE was -0.09%, meaning no photoactivity.
Close to CuV2O6 stoichiometry. EQE was only 0.026%, lower than the more V-rich index 46.

consultations.verdict: Support. MACE puts Cu3V2O8 near the hull (0.016 eV/atom), so it should form. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.67 eV looks too low; experimental Cu vanadate gaps are about 1.8–2.0 eV, which the 2.06 eV photons can excite. Index 114 is the most Cu-rich candidate and closest to a Cu3V2O8/Cu2V2O7 phase mixture.

Moderately supportive. MEGNet puts the V2O5 HSE gap at 2.83 eV, and its real gap (~2.3 eV) is at or above the 2.06 eV photons, so pure V-rich phases absorb weakly. Adding Cu narrows the gap (CuV2O6 is about 1.9–2.0 eV). The Cu-rich index 114 was inactive. Index 65 has Cu:V ≈ 0.54, close to CuV2O6 stoichiometry, which should balance absorption at 2.06 eV against a vanadate network.

Weak support. MACE puts V2O5 on the hull, so the V-rich region should hold a stable V2O5 or CuV2O6 mix. Activity has risen with V content so far (114 at -0.09, 65 at +0.026). Index 46 (Cu 0.18, V 0.63) moves further toward V-rich while keeping enough Cu for absorption below 2.06 eV, and the GP UCB ranks it in its top 5.
